goal: The scheduled full run is reached as `mc test nightly start | stop | status`, and `mc repo nightly` is gone. Martin, 2026-09-04: *"`mc repo` ska inte finnas som kommando. Det är legacy."* The nightly is the scheduled form of `mc test <repo> --full` — `nightly-run.js` calls the same `runGate` with `full: true` — so it belongs under the verb whose round it runs, not under a verb the verb list (`mc-cut`, #543) never named.

`mc test nightly status` also answers the question the nightly exists for — *red, and since when* — which today is printed only by `mc repo status`'s *full run* section (`repo-render.js:nightlyRows`). After this, a person reads it where they started it.

This project is one step and one pull request. It is small on purpose: `test-architecture`'s first state, `main-green` in memoro, is blocked on it, because its second step starts the nightly and reads it and must not do so through a legacy verb.
contract: The daemon does not change. `nightly.js`, `nightly-loop.js`, `nightly-run.js`, `nightly-history.js` — the pid file, the history under `~/.memoro/mc/nightly/`, the default interval, the lease it takes, the SIGTERM handling, what a run records — are untouched. This is a verb move and a reading, not a rewrite.

No alias. `mc repo nightly …` prints `mc repo nightly is now mc test nightly` and exits 2, the way `mc repo merge` has since 2026-08-26 (`docs/mc-command-matrix.md`). A legacy verb that still works is a verb nobody retires.

The rest of `mc repo` — `status`, `watch`, `claim`, `release`, `who`, `rounds`, `guard`, `push-check` — is not touched here. Its retirement is the verb list's question and belongs to `mc plan mc`, named in `docs/project/mc/rulings.md` if it is not already.
out_of_scope: Where the nightly's reading appears on the page (`mc`). The page shows no full-run line today, and whether it should is a page question; `mc test nightly status` is the reading this project delivers.
The other seven `mc repo` sub-verbs, and `repo.js`'s continued existence as the home of `gate` and `parseMergeArgs`, which `test.js` imports.
Starting the nightly. That is `main-green` step 2 in memoro, with Martin's machine and Martin's say.

success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/nightly.test.js`'s start/status/stop round-trip runs `mc test nightly …` instead of `mc repo nightly …` and passes; `mc repo nightly start` exits 2 with the pointer line and starts nothing, asserted in the same file.

success_criteria.criterion: `mc test nightly status` says red, and since when.
success_criteria.check: With a history file holding a red run, `mc test nightly status` prints, per repository: when the last measured run was, its commit, `N red of M`, and the oldest red test's name with the date its streak began; `--json` carries `running`, `interval_ms`, and per repository the `nightlyReading` object. Asserted on a fixture history in `tests/mc/nightly.test.js`.

success_criteria.criterion: Nothing in the repository still says `mc repo nightly`.
success_criteria.check: `git grep -n 'mc repo nightly' -- src docs canon README.md AGENTS.md` returns only the exit-2 pointer string and `docs/project/project_log.md`'s historical rows.

steps.title: mc test nightly, and mc repo nightly points at it
steps.done_when: `mc test nightly start [--interval <seconds>] | stop | status [--json]` does what `mc repo nightly …` did, and `status` additionally prints each repository's last measured run — when, commit, red of total, oldest red and since when — with `--json` carrying the same; `mc repo nightly …` exits 2 with `mc repo nightly is now mc test nightly`; `tests/mc/nightly.test.js` asserts both on the new arguments; `mc help`, `docs/mc-command-matrix.md`, `docs/technical/mc-merge.md`, `docs/technical/mc-cut.md` and every user-facing string under `src/` say the new verb; and `npm test` is green.
instruction: `src/mc/commands/test.js` hands everything to `parseMergeArgs(argv, { full: true })`, which reads the first positional as a repository name. Intercept before that: if `argv[0] === 'nightly'`, dispatch on `argv[1]` to the three sub-verbs and never reach `parseMergeArgs`. No repository is named `nightly` and none will be; say so in a comment rather than defending against it. Keep `test.js`'s existing header comment true — it already says the nightly runs this same round — and add the one sentence that it is now reached from here.

The three sub-verbs move whole from `src/mc/commands/repo.js:nightly` (lines 156–190 on 2026-09-04): `start` calls `startNightly` with the interval, `stop` calls `stopNightly`, `status` reads `nightlyState()`. Move the function and its `every()` helper rather than re-implement them; `repo.js` keeps `gate`, `parseMergeArgs`, the lease verbs and the rest. Take `'nightly'` out of `repo.js`'s `VERBS` and make the verb answer with the pointer and exit code 2 — `mc repo merge` in the same file is the pattern, and `docs/mc-command-matrix.md:63` is how it is documented. Fix `INTERVAL_ELSEWHERE` in `repo.js`, which names the old verb.

`status` gains the reading. `nightlyReading(repoPath)` in `src/mc/nightly-history.js` already computes it — `measured` (the last run that measured anything: `at`, `commit`, `tests`, `red`), `last` (the last attempt, which may be `incomplete`), `runs`, and `red[]` with each red test's name and the `since` its consecutive streak began — and `repo-render.js:nightlyRows` already renders it for `mc repo status`. Render the same rows under `mc test nightly status`, one block per repository mc knows (`resolveRepoPath` over the same list the loop iterates), below the running/interval/log lines that are printed today. Reuse `nightlyRows` by exporting it, or move it to a module both renderers import; do not write a second rendering that can drift. `--json` returns `{ running, pid, interval_ms, log, repos: { <name>: nightlyReading(...) } }` — the fields `nightlyState()` already returns plus the readings.

Strings. `repo-render.js` lines 123, 125 and 178 tell the reader to type `mc repo nightly …`; `help-text.js` lines 83–93 document the old verb under `mc repo` — move that block under `mc test`, next to `--full`, and shorten it: the long form belongs in `docs/technical/mc-merge.md` § *The full run nobody asks for*, which also has to say the new verb, as do `docs/technical/mc-cut.md` and `docs/mc-command-matrix.md`. `git grep -n 'mc repo nightly'` at the end is the check; the only survivors are the pointer string and `project_log.md`.

Tests. `tests/mc/nightly.test.js` drives the real CLI through `runMcCli(['repo', 'nightly', …])` at lines 215–257; change the arguments, and add two assertions: `mc repo nightly status` exits 2 and prints the pointer, and `mc test nightly status` over a fixture history file prints `N red of M` and the oldest red name with its since-date, and `--json` carries the reading. The fixture is a `mc-nightly-history` v1 file with two runs, the second red on a test the first was also red on, so *since when* is the first run's `at` and not the second's. `tests/mc/nightly-history.test.js` shows how one is written.

One trap, from `mc-workarea-deps`: this repository's tests run from `~/mc/node_modules` above the workarea, so a new import resolves the same way a test's does, but a new file under `src/` is not seen by `scripts/affected-tests.js` until it is `git add`ed. Add before running `npm test`.
comments: `'nightly'` stays in `repo.js`'s `VERBS`, which the instruction said to take it out of. It has to: the pointer is returned from `parseArgs`, exactly as `mc repo merge`'s is, and a word that is not in `VERBS` is read as a repository name — `mc repo nightly start` would then answer `no repository called "nightly"` and exit 1 instead of saying where the verb went. The comment above the list now says both spellings are kept only to be answered.

`mc test nightly status` lists one block per repository from `knownRepos()`, now exported from `nightly-loop.js` — literally the list a tick iterates, so the page cannot name a repository the loop never visits. It costs what `mc repo status --offline` costs (the board, plus git per repository); the rows themselves are `repo-render.js`'s own `nightlyRows`, called by both renderers rather than copied.

`git grep -n 'mc repo nightly' -- src docs canon README.md AGENTS.md` returns four lines: the pointer string in `repo.js`, the matrix's *Gone* row and `mc-merge.md`'s sentence (both quoting that string), and two prose mentions of the move as history — `commands/test.js`'s header and `mc-merge.md:437`. Nothing tells a reader to type it. The unreleased `changelog.d/the-full-run-nobody-asks-for.md` was renamed too, since it would otherwise announce a verb that does not exist.
